weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_write.go.when: PutObject, CompleteMultipartUpload, DeleteObject (unversioned fast path), CopyObject onto itself, and versioned finalize paths call these when routableWriteOwner returns an owner; with no objectWriteLockClient the callers fall back to the distributed-lock path and plain mkFile.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_routed_write.go.why: Design: all writes to one object (versioned, suspended or not) share one route key and owner, so they serialize under one path lock and conditional writes (If-Match, If-None-Match: *) are checked atomically at the filer instead of racing in the gateway. A trailing-slash marker key ('dir/') hashes to the same owner as 'dir'. Transactions are not replayable: failover only crosses a channel that never came up, and each logical transaction carries one RequestId so a retry replays the recorded outcome instead of re-applying mutations. Multipart completion removes the upload directory inside the same transaction, with an upload-exists precondition, so an abort/lifecycle/s3.clean.uploads that removed the directory first fails the commit instead of publishing an object over freed chunks. Consequence: with a ring configured, this is how every routed object write lands.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.character: S3ApiServer helpers that resolve the ACL an object upload will carry (stashed in the request context) plus a stateless request rewriter for policy evaluation
gotchas: When auth is disabled but a bucket policy exists, an explicit ACL is still checked against the policy for both Write and WriteAcp.
putObjectACLPolicyRequest only rewrites requests that resolve to s3:PutObject; other actions pass through unchanged.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.if_broken: Objects are stored with the wrong owner or grants (public by mistake, or unreadable by the bucket owner), or ACL-conditioned bucket policies can be bypassed.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.ux: x-amz-acl / x-amz-grant-* on uploads behave like AWS's, including on presigned URLs; clear InvalidRequest / AccessControlListNotSupported errors.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.what: preparePutObjectACL runs before the object bytes are stored. It reads the canned ACL and x-amz-grant-* values from headers AND (for SigV4 presigned URLs) the query string, where presigners hoist signed headers; it rejects conflicting duplicates, requires s3:PutObjectAcl for any explicit ACL, applies the bucket's ownership mode (BucketOwnerEnforced only accepts private / bucket-owner-full-control and makes the bucket owner the owner), always grants the owner FULL_CONTROL on custom grants, and stashes the resulting owner/grant Extended attributes in the request context. applyPutObjectACL copies them onto the new entry. putObjectACLPolicyRequest builds a cloned request whose ACL headers carry the effective (query-hoisted, normalized) values so bucket-policy conditions such as s3:x-amz-acl evaluate the ACL the object will actually get, keeping the original values for s3:x-amz-grant-* conditions.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.when: PutObject (regular and directory-marker paths), CreateMultipartUpload and other upload paths that call preparePutObjectACL before writing; putObjectACLPolicyRequest from iam.Auth (authRequestWithAuthType) and checkPolicyWithEntry.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_upload_acl.go.why: Consequence: without this, a presigned URL could set an ACL through the query string that policy evaluation never saw (bypassing a 'Deny unless x-amz-acl=private' policy), or ACLs would be accepted on BucketOwnerEnforced buckets where AWS rejects them. Design: the ACL is computed once, before the upload, so a rejected ACL fails fast instead of after the body was stored; the context key cannot be set by clients. AWS compatibility: AccessControlListNotSupported for disallowed ACLs on BucketOwnerEnforced buckets; SigV2 requests ignore query-borne ACL values; canned and grant headers are mutually exclusive.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.character: S3ApiServer methods that build ObjectTransaction mutations for versioned writes and deletes on the key's owner filer (the routed counterpart of the gateway-side pointer updates in s3api_object_versioning.go)
gotchas: objectWriteOwner here and routableWriteOwner in s3api_object_routed_write.go both resolve the owner from the same route key; keep them in sync.
routedDeleteNullVersion falls back to the lock path on any transport or transaction error (deletes are idempotent), while routedDeleteSpecificVersion fails the request instead.
routedMultipartFinalize keeps a gateway-side upload-exists check for older filers that ignore the mutation's condition.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.if_broken: Latest pointers drift from the actual newest version, locked versions get deleted, or completed uploads leave their staging directories behind.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.ux: Read-after-write correct 'latest' in multi-filer clusters; AccessDenied when a versioned delete hits a locked version.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.what: latestPointerRecompute builds a RECOMPUTE_LATEST mutation: the filer scans <key>.versions/ (descending or ascending by version-id format), writes the winner's file name, size and mtime plus copies of its version id / ETag / owner / delete-marker / storage class onto the .versions entry, and optionally stamps NoncurrentSinceNs on the demoted version. On top of it: routedVersionedFinalize (delete markers), routedMultipartFinalize (PUT the version file + delete the upload dir + recompute, guarded by an upload-exists precondition), routedDeleteSpecificVersion (recompute only if the deleted file was current, then delete, under a WORM condition), routedDeleteNullVersion, versionedFinalize (a putFinalize that rides inside putToFiler's transaction, with an off-ring afterCreate fallback), finalizeSuspendedNullWrite, and wormDeleteCondition (legal hold not ON AND retention-until elapsed; with bypass, the retention clause is gated to COMPLIANCE only).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.when: Versioned PutObject / CopyObject (via putToFiler's finalize), CompleteMultipartUpload on versioned buckets, versioned DeleteObject with or without versionId, delete-marker creation, suspended-versioning null writes, whenever objectWriteOwner/routableWriteOwner returns an owner.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioned_finali.why: Consequence: with a filer ring, these transactions are what keep the version file and the latest pointer consistent; without atomicity a crash or a concurrent writer leaves latest pointing at a missing or older version. Design: putting the version PUT, the pointer recompute and (for multipart) the upload-dir removal in ONE transaction under the object path lock means readers never see a half-finalized version; WORM conditions are evaluated by the filer under that same lock, so a retention set concurrently cannot be raced past. The off-ring path keeps the older lock-and-update behavior. AWS compatibility: governance bypass lifts only GOVERNANCE retention, never COMPLIANCE or legal hold.

weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioning.go.character: S3ApiServer methods implementing the on-filer versioning model (versions stored as <key>.versions/v_<id> files plus a latest-version pointer on the .versions directory entry), the ListObjectVersions handler, and a per-request filer retry budget
gotchas: deleteSpecificObjectVersion(versionId='null') treats ANY getEntry error (including transient ones) as 'already gone' and returns success without deleting.
getLatestObjectVersion retries the .versions lookup 8 times with 100ms·2^n backoff (worst case ~12.7s); conditional-header checks use the 1-retry fast path instead.
versionIdFromEntry falls back to the 'v_' file-name prefix when the entry has no version-id metadata.

The cached latest-version metadata on .versions/ is what listings trust; any writer that moves the pointer must call setCachedListMetadata or clearCachedVersionMetadata or listings show the old size/ETag.
processExplicitDirectory reports explicit directory markers as a 'null' version with the empty-content ETag d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioning.go.if_broken: Deleted objects reappear, the wrong version is served as current, ListObjectVersions duplicates or drops versions across pages, or lifecycle NoncurrentDays expiration fires at the wrong time.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioning.go.ux: x-amz-version-id semantics, delete markers, IsLatest flags and ordering in list-object-versions output, and whether deleting the latest version makes the previous one visible again.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioning.go.what: Owns the versioned storage layout: createDeleteMarker / createNullDeleteMarker write marker files under <key>.versions/ and move the latest pointer (routed RECOMPUTE_LATEST when a ring owner exists); getSpecificObjectVersion / doGetLatestObjectVersion resolve a version or the current one; deleteSpecificObjectVersion repoints latest BEFORE deleting the version it names; updateLatestVersionAfterDeletion, healStaleLatestVersionPointer, clearStaleLatestVersionPointer and recoverLatestVersionWithoutPointer rescan .versions/ to repair a pointer naming a missing file, guarded by IF_ENTRY_EQUAL so a concurrent move is never overwritten. setCachedListMetadata copies the latest version's size/mtime/ETag/owner/storage-class/delete-marker onto the .versions entry so listings need one scan. ListObjectVersionsHandler walks the bucket (versionCollector with marker, prefix, delimiter and an early-stop bound) and interleaves Version/DeleteMarker/CommonPrefixes in AWS order. retryFilerOp retries transient filer errors 6 times (100ms doubling, capped at 2s) inside a shared per-request budget.
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioning.go.when: GET/HEAD/DELETE/PUT on versioned or suspended buckets (via the object handlers and putVersionedObject), GET /bucket?versions, the versioning reconciler, and listing code that reads the cached latest metadata (getLatestVersionEntryFromDirectoryEntry).
weed/s3api/s3api_object_versioning.go.why: Consequence: this is the version history of every versioned bucket; a wrong pointer either resurrects a deleted object, hides the current one, or serves an old version. Design: the pointer moves before the version file is deleted so a crash in between never leaves latest naming a missing file; any stale pointer that does appear (replication lag, crashes) self-heals on read with an IF_ENTRY_EQUAL write and, failing that, is queued for the background versioning reconciler. NoncurrentSinceNs is stamped on the demoted version BEFORE the pointer flip, because the lifecycle router reacts to the flip's metadata event and would otherwise derive the age from a sibling's mtime (wrong for versioned copies). A suspended-versioning delete collapses onto one 'null' marker (v_null) rather than accumulating markers, per the S3 spec. AWS compatibility: ListObjectVersions sorts by key, then newest version first, interleaving the three element kinds; max-keys caps at 1000 and max-keys=0 returns an empty, non-truncated page.

weed/s3api/s3api_put_handlers.go.character: S3ApiServer methods: the single SSE dispatch point for writes (SSE-C, SSE-KMS, SSE-S3, single-part and multipart) and the SSE-metadata writer for entries
gotchas: Order matters: the three handlers are applied in sequence on the same reader; request validation elsewhere must keep SSE-C and SSE-KMS/S3 mutually exclusive, or data would be double-encrypted.
Fixing the IV scheme requires a matching change in completedMultipartChunk (filer_multipart.go) and must stay readable for objects already written with partOffset 0.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_handlers.go.if_broken: Encrypted objects become unreadable, or are encrypted unsafely.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_handlers.go.issue_note: SSE-S3 multipart parts reuse the AES-CTR keystream. handleSSES3MultipartEncryption encrypts every part with the upload's single shared DEK and CreateSSES3EncryptedReaderWithBaseIV(baseIV, partOffset), and putToFiler always passes partOffset = 0 (s3api_object_handlers_put.go; completedMultipartChunk in filer_multipart.go documents and depends on this). So byte k of every part is XORed with the same keystream byte, and anyone with read access to the stored chunks (the threat SSE-S3 exists for) can XOR two parts to obtain the XOR of their plaintexts. s3_constants.PartOffsetMultiplier, documented as preventing exactly this, is never used. SSE-KMS is unaffected (fresh data key per part) and SSE-C uses a random IV per part.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_handlers.go.ux: Invisible when correct: clients get the matching SSE response headers and can read their data back.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_handlers.go.what: handleAllSSEEncryption chains the three handlers over the body reader and reports which type applied. handleSSECEncryption parses the customer key and encrypts with a random IV; handleSSEKMSEncryption builds the encryption context (bucket/key plus any user context) and either encrypts with a fresh data key and random IV, or, for multipart parts (SeaweedFSSSEKMSBaseIVHeader set by the part handler), with a fresh data key and the upload's base IV advanced by partOffset; handleSSES3Encryption encrypts single-part objects with a fresh DEK and random IV, or multipart parts with the upload's shared DEK (SeaweedFSSSES3KeyDataHeader) and base IV advanced by partOffset. storeSSEMetadata writes the object-level SSE keys (IV and key MD5 for SSE-C, serialized key metadata plus algorithm/key id for SSE-KMS and SSE-S3).
weed/s3api/s3api_put_handlers.go.when: putToFiler (PutObject, UploadPart, copy destinations) and the directory-marker path of PutObjectHandler.
weed/s3api/s3api_put_handlers.go.why: Consequence: every encrypted write goes through here; it decides the IV and key each byte is encrypted with, and therefore whether reads can decrypt and whether the encryption is sound. Design: multipart parameters are injected as internal headers by the part handler so one code path serves PutObject and UploadPart; SSE-KMS uses a new data key per call, so reusing an IV across parts is harmless there. AWS compatibility: SSE-C, SSE-KMS (with x-amz-server-side-encryption-context) and SSE-S3 behave as in AWS from the client's point of view.

weed/s3api/s3api_server.go.character: The composition root: S3ApiServerOption (flags), the S3ApiServer struct every handler hangs off, its constructor and the mux route table; plus the bucket-policy recheck helpers handlers call after loading an entry
gotchas: Inserting a route in the wrong position silently shadows others; follow the ordering rule in the comment at the top of the per-bucket route block.
PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration / DeleteBucketLifecycle require ACTION_ADMIN (#12327), unlike most bucket config writes, which use ACTION_WRITE.
Ownership-controls routes skip cb.Limit (they are wrapped only in iam.Auth).
ValidateS3Credential compares the secret with != (not constant time); lance/handlers_oauth.go uses it for OAuth client_credentials and token verification.

STS has its own routes plus a lowest-priority unauthenticated POST / fallback; signed POST / goes to UnifiedPostHandler, which dispatches on Action (AssumeRole*/GetCallerIdentity/GetFederationToken to STS, everything else to embedded IAM).
recheckPolicyForKeyWithLookup is deny-biased: any lookup miss or error keeps the original Deny, and an explicit Deny in the caller's own policies still vetoes a bucket-policy Allow.
weed/s3api/s3api_server.go.if_broken: The gateway does not start, or routes land on the wrong handler (for example a tagging PUT treated as a PutObject that overwrites the object). If the lock-ring subscription were lost, route-by-key writes would silently fall back to the distributed lock path.
weed/s3api/s3api_server.go.ux: Defines which URL shapes work (path-style vs virtual-host via -domainName, health probes at /status, /healthz, /readyz), which operations exist, and the defaults: no IAM config means 'no credentials = allow all' so `docker run seaweedfs` works out of the box (#9557), while an explicit IAM config file defaults to Deny.
weed/s3api/s3api_server.go.what: NewS3ApiServerWithStore wires the whole gateway: legacy IAM (IdentityAccessManagement), bucket policy engine, FilerClient (with master-based filer discovery when -master is given), the object-write lock ring (LockClient fed by master LockRingUpdates), the SSE-S3 key manager, a shared ReaderCache for GET streaming (256 downloader slots, optional in-memory chunk cache), circuit breaker, bucket config cache (60 min TTL), optional advanced IAM + STS + embedded IAM API, trusted proxies, SIGHUP reload hooks, and the background loops (metadata subscription, bucket size metrics, owner-index backfill, versioning reconciler). registerRouter declares every S3 route on gorilla/mux: path-style and virtual-host routers per -domainName plus a host-less catch-all, each wrapped as track(iam.Auth(cb.Limit(handler, ACTION))). It also holds checkPolicyWithEntry / recheck*Policy*, which re-run bucket-policy evaluation once a handler has the object's entry (for s3:ExistingObjectTag conditions), and small adapters other servers use (AuthenticateRequest, ValidateS3Credential, GetCredentialByAccessKey).
weed/s3api/s3api_server.go.when: Constructed once at process start by weed/command (s3, filer -s3, mini); registerRouter runs inside the constructor. The recheck helpers run inside object handlers after the entry is fetched. SIGHUP re-reads the -config identities, the JWT filer signing keys and the trusted proxies.
weed/s3api/s3api_server.go.why: Design: route order is load-bearing: gorilla/mux picks the first match, so object routes with a query come before plain object routes, those before bucket routes with a query, and plain bucket routes come last. ListObjectsV1 is the catch-all GET and explicitly answers NotImplemented for unrouted subresources instead of returning a listing. The lock client subscribes to ring updates BEFORE the master loop starts because the master sends the initial LockRingUpdate only once per connect. The advertised host must be -ip, not a wildcard bind address, or IAM pushes from peers dial an unroutable address and fail silently after 10s. The auth path primes bucket loads (iam.primeBucketForIAM) because advanced-IAM evaluates the bucket-policy mirror before any handler runs, and a grant carried only by a not-yet-mirrored policy would otherwise deny forever. Consequence: everything else in the package is reached from here.

weed/s3api/s3api_version_id.go.character: Stateless helpers (plus two thin S3ApiServer path methods) defining the version-id format and its ordering
gotchas: Do not compare version ids with plain string comparison: old- and new-format ids sort in opposite directions; always use compareVersionIds.
If crypto/rand fails, the random half falls back to 16 zeros (logged), so ids generated in the same nanosecond could collide.
weed/s3api/s3api_version_id.go.if_broken: Latest-version selection picks the wrong version (older data served as current, deleted objects resurrected), or a crafted versionId escapes the .versions directory.
weed/s3api/s3api_version_id.go.ux: Clients see 32-hex-char x-amz-version-id values; ListObjectVersions orders newest first.
weed/s3api/s3api_version_id.go.what: generateVersionId builds a 32-hex-char id: 16 hex of a nanosecond timestamp plus 16 hex of crypto randomness. The NEW format stores MaxInt64−now ('inverted', so newer ids sort first lexicographically); the OLD format stores now directly. isNewFormatVersionId tells them apart by the 0x4000000000000000 threshold, compareVersionIds orders any mix (same format: lexicographic, in the right direction; mixed: by decoded timestamp; 'null' always last), getVersionIdFormat keeps an object on the format its .versions/ latest pointer already uses (defaults to new). Also getVersionedObjectDir (<bucket>/<key>.versions), getVersionFileName (v_<id>), isValidVersionID (a safe single path segment).
weed/s3api/s3api_version_id.go.when: Every versioned write (putVersionedObject, delete markers, versioned copy/complete), every latest-version selection, and validation of any client-supplied versionId.
weed/s3api/s3api_version_id.go.why: Consequence: version ids are filer path segments and the sort key for 'latest' everywhere (pointer recompute, ListObjectVersions, NoncurrentVersion lifecycle); a wrong comparison promotes an old version to current. Design: inverted timestamps make the filer's natural ascending listing return newest first, so finding the latest needs no full scan, while objects whose history predates the change keep their old ascending format so their ordering stays consistent. isValidVersionID rejects '/', '\', '.', '..' because a version id becomes a filename under .versions/ (path traversal). AWS compatibility: AWS version ids are opaque strings; 'null' is the reserved id for unversioned / suspended writes.

weed/s3api/s3err/.character: Leaf package: S3 error codes (ErrorCode enum mapped to APIError{Code, Description, HTTPStatus}), the XML response writers, and the Fluent access/audit logger (a package-global Logger)
gotchas: Every new ErrorCode MUST get an errorCodeResponse entry: GetAPIError is a plain map lookup with no default, and a missing entry makes WriteHeader(0) panic.

getRemoteIP trusts X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP as-is for the audit log (unlike the policy engine, which honors only configured trusted proxies), so the logged remote_ip is client-spoofable unless the proxy strips these headers.
WriteResponse type-asserts w.(http.Flusher); a ResponseWriter wrapper that does not implement Flusher panics.
PostAccessLog skips records with an empty Key.
weed/s3api/s3err/.if_broken: Clients receive wrong statuses or malformed errors, so retries, 404 handling and conditional logic fail; or audit entries go missing or are duplicated.
weed/s3api/s3err/.issue_note: ErrMalformedCredentialDate (declared in the ErrorCode enum) has no entry in errorCodeResponse, so GetAPIError returns a zero APIError (status 0) and WriteErrorResponse panics with 'invalid WriteHeader code 0'. Reachable without credentials: any request whose SigV4 Authorization header (or presigned X-Amz-Credential, or POST-policy credential) carries a Credential date that does not parse returns this code from parseCredentialHeader (auth_signature_v4.go), and iam.Auth hands it straight to WriteErrorResponse before any key lookup. Reproduced end to end against this commit with a throwaway test calling iam.Auth: the handler panics; under net/http the panic is recovered per connection, so the client sees a dropped connection instead of a 400 AuthorizationQueryParametersError.
weed/s3api/s3err/.ux: The exact XML error body, HTTP status and x-amz-request-id every client receives; the audit trail operators query.
weed/s3api/s3err/.what: Defines ~110 ErrorCode values and errorCodeResponse, the map to AWS error codes and HTTP statuses. WriteErrorResponse(WithMessage) builds the AWS RESTErrorResponse XML (Code, Message, Resource, RequestId, Key, BucketName), drains the request body for up to 30s, writes, and posts an audit entry. WriteXMLResponse/WriteAwsXMLResponse/WriteEmptyResponse/WriteResponse set x-amz-request-id and Accept-Ranges, apply fallback CORS headers on service-level requests, and suppress bodies for HEAD/1xx/204/304. audit_fluent.go builds AccessLog records (requester, principal ARN, OIDC claim, access key id, operation like REST.PUT.OBJECT, error code) and posts them asynchronously to Fluent, with a per-request flag so the track() middleware can emit a fallback entry without double-logging.
weed/s3api/s3err/.when: At the end of every request: errors from auth, the circuit breaker and handlers; success writers through s3api_handlers.go. InitAuditLog runs once when -auditLogConfig is set.
weed/s3api/s3err/.why: Consequence: every error any S3 client sees is shaped here; SDKs branch on the XML Code (NoSuchKey, SlowDown, PreconditionFailed…), so a wrong code or status breaks retries and existence checks. Design: the request body is drained on error so the client, which may still be streaming an upload, gets the error response instead of a connection reset. The audit 'already logged' flag lets handlers that log themselves coexist with the generic fallback. AWS compatibility: codes and statuses follow the AWS ErrorResponses table; several SeaweedFS-specific codes reuse AWS codes (InvalidArgument for bad directives).
